attributes.protocol: ViroBench classification, ALL viruses, Host, G-Split; score is Macro-F1 as printed in Table 25
limitations: The benchmark authors ran every model, including their own in-house ViroHyena, ViroDNABERT2 and ViroCaduceus models and the BiLSTM and CNN baselines.

Results are the mean (standard deviation) across hyperparameter settings (window sizes 512, 1024 and 2048 with 8, 4 and 2 sampled windows, and learning rates 1e-2 to 1e-4), not across random seeds (Section 4.1.2).
Values are printed without a unit; the ablation tables state Macro-F1 in %, so they are recorded as percent.

evidence_concerns.message: Table 25 prints one Macro-F1 per model for the taxonomy columns. For 143 of the 144 model-by-split taxonomy cells on the ALL-virus set, the printed value equals the mean of the five per-rank values in Table 26 rounded to two decimals. The exception is RNA-FM under the genus-disjoint split: Table 25 prints 48.67 and the mean of the Table 26 ranks (59.96, 65.35, 37.58, 58.78, 43.82) is 53.10. One of the two tables is wrong for that row, so RNA-FM ALL taxonomy G-Split should not be used in a comparison without checking the published code.

Pretraining coverage is the paper's main explanatory variable, so NT v3 rows should not be used to support a coverage-versus-performance claim.
